git-fundamentals-sr2-02.reason: weak_card, rewritten instead of dropped: dropping 01, 02, 04 and 08 would leave r2 with 8 cards. The verifier's replacement tests HEAD as a symref, shortened so that r2 true and false lengths stay within 5 (T 77.0 / F 74.0). Checked on gitglossary (symref: 'of the format ref: refs/some/thing ... HEAD is a prime example of a symref'; detached HEAD: 'Normally the HEAD stores the name of a branch'). (final: keep)
git-fundamentals-sr2-02.statement: On a branch, HEAD holds refs/heads/<branch> rather than a commit ID.
git-fundamentals-sr2-02.explanation: gitglossary calls HEAD the prime example of a symref: it holds ref: refs/heads/<branch>, and Git dereferences it to that branch, which holds the commit ID.

git-fundamentals-sr2-05.reason: ambiguous: the glossary defines pseudorefs by their write restriction, not by holding several IDs. The new card follows the verifier's fix, shortened for length balance. gitglossary (last updated in 2.56.0): 'These refs can be read via normal Git commands, but cannot be written to by commands like git-update-ref'; FETCH_HEAD and MERGE_HEAD are the listed pseudorefs. The card is attributed to gitglossary because the git-update-ref page still calls HEAD and ORIG_HEAD pseudorefs. (final: fixed)
git-fundamentals-sr2-05.statement: gitglossary describes pseudorefs as refs that git update-ref treats as read-only.
git-fundamentals-sr2-05.explanation: gitglossary lists FETCH_HEAD and MERGE_HEAD as pseudorefs: refs with different semantics from normal refs, readable through ordinary Git commands but not writable with git update-ref.

git-fundamentals-sr4-10.reason: weak_card, rewritten instead of dropped: dropping 03, 04 and 10 would leave r4 at 3T/6F. The verifier's replacement is used. git-branch (last updated in 2.56.0): '-m --move Move/rename a branch, together with its config and reflog' and 'If <old-branch> had a corresponding reflog, it is renamed to match <new-branch>, and a reflog entry is created to remember the branch renaming.' (final: keep)
git-fundamentals-sr4-10.statement: git branch -m carries the branch's reflog and its branch.<name> settings over to the new name.
git-fundamentals-sr4-10.explanation: Renaming moves the branch's configuration, such as its upstream, and renames its reflog, adding an entry that records the rename. The commits themselves are untouched.

git-fundamentals-sr6-05.reason: weak_card, rewritten instead of dropped: dropping 01, 05, 09 and 11 would leave r6 with 8 cards (3T/5F). The verifier's replacement is reworded so that it does not copy the source sentence. git-rebase (last updated in 2.54.0): 'By default, a rebase will simply drop merge commits from the todo list, and put the rebased commits into a single, linear branch. With --rebase-merges ... recreating the merge commits. Any resolved merge conflicts or manual amendments in these merge commits will have to be resolved/re-applied manually.' The page also names rebase.rebaseMerges. (final: keep)
git-fundamentals-sr6-05.statement: By default, git rebase linearizes the replayed range, leaving its merge commits out of the new history.
git-fundamentals-sr6-05.explanation: Rebase drops merge commits from the todo list unless --rebase-merges or rebase.rebaseMerges asks it to recreate them; manual resolutions in those merges must then be redone.

git-fundamentals-sr11-12.reason: weak_card, rewritten instead of dropped: dropping 04, 08, 11 and 12 would leave r11 with 8 cards (3T/5F). The verifier's replacement (empty-source refspec) is used, shortened for length balance. git-push: 'If <src> is empty, it deletes the <dst> ref from the remote repository. For example, git push origin :dev will delete the dev branch.' --delete: 'This is the same as prefixing all refs with a colon.' (final: keep)
git-fundamentals-sr11-12.statement: git push origin :topic, with its empty source, deletes the branch topic on the remote.
git-fundamentals-sr11-12.explanation: A refspec with an empty <src> deletes the <dst> ref from the remote repository, the same as git push --delete origin topic.

git-fundamentals-sr12-12.reason: explanation_error: the old explanation implied that only ^0 makes a fast-forward possible. git-merge's --ff paragraph says --no-ff is assumed only for an annotated tag outside refs/tags/. The new explanation relies only on what the page states consistently: the MERGING TAG section advises unwrapping with ^0, and gitrevisions says '<rev>^0 means the commit itself and is used when <rev> is the object name of a tag object that refers to a commit object'. The statement is unchanged. (final: keep)
git-fundamentals-sr12-12.statement: git merge --ff v1.2^0 can fast-forward to the commit behind an annotated v1.2 tag.
git-fundamentals-sr12-12.explanation: v1.2^0 peels the annotated tag to the commit it points to, so git merge sees a plain commit and fast-forwards when the current tip is its ancestor. git-merge suggests ^0 to catch up to a tagged release.

git-fundamentals-sr2-10.statement: For divergent tips A and B, git log A...B selects history unique to either side.
git-fundamentals-sr2-10.explanation: In git log, A...B includes commits reachable from A or B and excludes commits reachable from both.
